questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Kazakhstan?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Kazakhstan article.

questions.proof: Astana is the capital city of Kazakhstan.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It means that Kazakhstan was not part of _____ anymore, but it was still in the Soviet Union.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “anymore”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Kazakhstan article, under the heading “Kazakh SSR”.

questions.proof: Kirghiz Autonomous Socialist Soviet Republic was created in Soviet Russian Republic of the Soviet Union (USSR) .

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The country declared its independence on 16 December _____, exactly five years after the beginning of Jeltoqsan unrest.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Independence” part of the Kazakhstan article.

questions.proof: The country declared its independence on 16 December 1991, exactly five years after the beginning of Jeltoqsan unrest.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “In December _____, the leader of Kazakh SSR Dinmukhamed Konayev was replaced by Gennady Kolbin, who was not from Kazakhstan.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Kazakh SSR” part of the Kazakhstan article.

questions.proof: In December 1986, the leader of Kazakh SSR Dinmukhamed Konayev was replaced by Gennady Kolbin, who was not from Kazakhstan.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It was named Kirghiz because Russians called Kazakhs "Kirghiz" before _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Kazakh SSR” part of the Kazakhstan article.

questions.proof: It was named Kirghiz because Russians called Kazakhs "Kirghiz" before 1925.
